sentences.en: [Alice] Hi, I'd like to check in, please.
[Bob] May I have your name?
[Alice] I have a reservation under the name Yoo.
[Alice] Is breakfast included in the room rate?
[Bob] Yes, it is. Anything else?
sentences.ko: 네, 포함되어 있어요. 더 필요하신 건요?

sentences.en: [Alice] Could I get a wake-up call at seven, please?
[Alice] Also, I need to print out my boarding pass.
[Bob] No problem, we have a printer in the lobby.
[Phone rings — Chris calls]
[Chris] Hey Alice, how have you been holding up?
sentences.ko: 안녕 Alice, 요즘 잘 버티고 있어?

sentences.en: [Alice] It's freezing cold outside today, but I'm okay.
sentences.ko: 오늘 밖이 진짜 춥지만 난 괜찮아.

sentences.en: [Alice] To be honest, I overslept this morning.
[Alice] You know I'm not a morning person.
sentences.ko: 내가 아침형 인간 아닌 거 알잖아.

sentences.en: [Chris] Ha! Let's keep in touch this week, okay?
sentences.ko: 하하! 이번 주에 계속 연락하고 지내자, 알았지?

sentences.en: [Next morning — at the hotel exit]
[Alice] Excuse me, could you point me in the right direction?
sentences.ko: 실례합니다, 어느 쪽으로 가야 하는지 알려주실 수 있나요?

sentences.en: [Bob] The conference center? It's about ten minutes away.
[Alice] Is it within walking distance?
[Bob] Yes, but a taxi would be faster.
sentences.ko: 네, 그런데 택시가 더 빠를 거예요.

sentences.en: [Alice] How long does it take to get there by taxi?
sentences.ko: 택시로 거기까지 가는 데 얼마나 걸려요?

sentences.en: [Alice — to taxi driver] Could you drop me off at the corner?
[Alice] I'm running out of time before the meeting.
[Quick email to colleague]
[Alice] Hi, I'm just dropping you a line to check in.
[Alice] Could you keep me in the loop on this?
sentences.ko: 이 건 진행 상황을 계속 공유해 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.en: [Alice] Unfortunately, I'm afraid I have to cancel our meeting.
sentences.ko: 아쉽지만, 죄송하지만 미팅을 취소해야 할 것 같아요.

sentences.en: [Alice] Let's hammer out the details tomorrow instead.
[Alice] I'll get back to you by end of day.
[Back home — meeting Chris at a cafe]
[Chris] You look tired. Cheer up, things will get better.
sentences.ko: 피곤해 보이네. 기운 내, 다 잘될 거야.

sentences.en: [Chris] Don't take it personally — work happens.
sentences.ko: 너무 개인적으로 받아들이지 마 — 일이 그런 거야.

sentences.en: [Chris] I'm here for you whenever you need me.
sentences.ko: 필요할 땐 언제든 내가 곁에 있을게.

sentences.en: [Alice] Thanks. I need to wind down before bed tonight.
sentences.ko: 고마워. 오늘 밤엔 자기 전에 긴장을 좀 풀어야 해.

sentences.en: [Alice] I always doze off on the couch after dinner.
sentences.ko: 저녁 먹고 나면 항상 소파에서 꾸벅꾸벅 졸아.

sentences.en: [At the supermarket]
[Alice] Excuse me, where can I find the dairy aisle?
[Dana] Aisle 4, on your right.
[Alice] Thanks. We're running low on milk at home.
sentences.ko: 감사합니다. 집에 우유가 거의 다 떨어져 가요.

sentences.en: [Alice] I need to stock up on groceries this weekend.
sentences.ko: 이번 주말에 식료품을 잔뜩 사둬야 해요.

sentences.en: [At checkout]
[Alice] Could you ring me up, please?
[Dana] Sure. Do you have a loyalty card I can sign up for?
sentences.ko: 네. 가입할 수 있는 멤버십 카드 있으세요?

sentences.en: [Alice] Yes, please. That sounds great.
